      <description>En buss kjørte i dag tidlig av veien i Røn i Vestre Slidre.
Politiet opplyser at bussen skal ha sklidd av veien i lav hastighet, men at den ligger på siden.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/skolebuss-av-veien-i-larvik-1.18079991</link>
      <description>Nødetatene har fått melding om en skolebuss som har kjørt av veien i Larvik.
– Bussen har sklidd av veien og ut i grøfta med alle fire hjul. I bussen er det 24 barn som fremstår uskadd, skriver operasjonsleder Per Magne Eftang i politiloggen.
Bussjåføren er også uskadd, ifølge politiet.
– Barna er nå på vei ut av bussen og inn et hus for å holde varmen, sier Eftang til NRK.
Han sier alle barna brukte bilbelte.
Operasjonslederen antar at hendelsen kan knyttes til det glatte føret, men politiet har ikke kommet fram til stedet ennå.
Klokka 09.44 opplyser politiet at ingen er skadet. Flere foreldre har hentet barna sine og ny buss er klar til å frakte resten av barna til skolen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/cnn_-demokratene-vinner-historisk-senatsvalg-i-mississippi-1.18079865</link>
      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>Klimaminister Sigrun Aasland (Ap) har med en stor sum når hun mandag reiser til åpningen av klimatoppmøtet i Tyrkia.

    <item>
      <title>Kongen fullførte maraton på tiden 4.43.01</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

      <title>Flere skadet etter kraftig jordskjelv sentralt i Japan</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

Fisheries and Oceans Canada says a landowner in B.C. is out more than $150,000 after they were ordered to restore a damaged fish habitat under the federal Fisheries Act.

]]>

Fisheries and Oceans Canada says a landowner in B.C. is out more than $150,000 after they were ordered to restore a damaged fish habitat under the federal Fisheries Act.

The landowner was ordered to pay for repairs under section 38(7.1) of the Fisheries Act after a contractor dug up fish habitat along Toboggan Creek near Smithers between Oct. 3 and Oct. 13, 2023, during what the DFO calls a “peak period for salmon migration and spawning.”

On Sept. 22, 2026, the contracted excavator operator was fined $26,100 for several offences related to the work, including three related to damaging fish habitat, one related to carrying out work without legal authorization, and one for failing to provide information requested by a fishery officer. 

On top of the fine, the contractor was ordered to forfeit a Bobcat excavator valued at approximately $50,000 that had been seized during the investigation.

The DFO says the landowner was not charged under the Fisheries Act since they cooperated through the investigation and paid approximately $155,000 for restoration work to the fish habitat.

The DFO describes Toboggan Creek as a “high value system” that’s used by coho salmon, pink salmon, rainbow trout, bull trout, steelhead, and other aquatic species.

“The Court found that digging up the creek bed, filling in the creek channel and removing vegetation along the banks damaged and destroyed fish habitat,” said Fisheries and Oceans Canada on Nov. 6.

“The work was carried out without the authorizations required under the Fisheries Act and the Water Sustainability Act.”

The DFO says it has resources on its website for people who are planning projects near water.

It also asks anyone who spots a suspected fisheries violation to contact the DFO Pacific Region at 1-800-465-4336, or email DFO.ORR-ONS.MPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca.

]]>

CHICAGO (AP) — A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant’s suite of apps.

Nearly 130,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.

Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.

Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications.

In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”

Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.

Microsoft did not immediately provide more information around what might be causing that failure, but added that it was testing a fix.

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X.

Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

Russian hockey federation president Vladislav Tretiak says Russia will seek compensation from Canada if its team is barred from next month’s world junior championship in Alberta.

The threat follows Ottawa’s statement Wednesday that Russian players will not be permitted to compete, even if they already hold valid Canadian visas, despite last month’s Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling ordering Russia’s reinstatement to international hockey.

Russia’s state news agency TASS reported Thursday that Tretiak told a presidential sports council meeting Russia would demand compensation from Canada and Germany, host of the 2027 men’s world championship, if denied participation. He also threatened to push for the tournaments to be moved and seek sanctions against organizers.

Tretiak, a legendary Soviet goaltender and three-time Olympic gold medallist, told TASS the federation had asked the International Ice Hockey Federation’s ethics council to investigate and punish national federations organizing boycotts of games against Russia.

Russian President Vladimir Putin told the same sports council meeting that national federations were refusing matches against Russian teams under pressure from their governments, according to TASS, which did not identify the countries involved.

Several hockey federations, including Finland, Sweden, Czechia and Norway, have said their teams will refuse to face Russia. The world juniors begin Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 12, 2026.

Heading into the wet and snowy season, WorkSafeBC is calling on employers and workers to be cautious to prevent the typical spike in slips, trips and falls.

The post Injuries from slips, trips and falls spike by 37% in winter months: WorkSafeBC appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Heading into the wet and snowy season, WorkSafeBC is calling on employers and workers to be cautious to prevent the typical spike in slips, trips and falls.

The work safety agency says that between November and March, injuries from slips, trips and falls increases by 37 per cent.

Injuries from these account for almost 7,000 accepted claims each year, which is about 12 per cent of all accepted claims.

Between 2021 and 2025, 11 workers died as a result of falls on the same level.

“These incidents are among the most common workplace injuries in B.C. Employers play an important role in making sure workers can move through the workplace safely,” says Todd McDonald, head of prevention services at WorkSafeBC.

“Regular inspections, prompt cleanup, good housekeeping practices, proper footwear, and involving workers in identifying risks can make a meaningful difference.”

WorkSafeBC says injuries from slips, trips and falls result in a loss of 500,000 workdays and more than $200 million in annual claim costs.

Slips, trips and falls can result in sprains, strains, fractures, concussions and other serious injuries.

WorkSafeBC urges employees to check for hazards, implement controls and monitor workplace health and safety risks.

Some things to implement are:

  • Installing electrical wires, cords and hoses where they aren’t tripping hazards.
  • Install covers, drip pans, containers or containment rooms to prevent the release of contaminants to the floor.
  • Store all tools, equipment and materials in designated locations.
  • Ensure workers are using appropriate footwear.

The BC SPCA is seeking donations after it rescued more than a dozen cats and kittens and one “severely neglected dog” from a property on Vancouver Island.

The SPCA did not say where on the Island the animals were rescued from, but said it was called to the area on Oct. 2 for a complaint about a severely matted dog and a large number of cats.

When the SPCA arrived, its animal protection officers found the dog tethered outside with a “heavily matted” coat that was causing her pain and restricting her movement. 

The dog, named Betty, lacked adequate food and water and was living in a small wooden doghouse that had two of its sides missing and was full of debris.

Once inside the house, the SPCA found the 14 cats and kittens, which were “visibly underweight with missing fur and distended bellies.”

“The owner was clearly overwhelmed and needed our help. The house was in poor condition; the floors were covered in filth and feces, and a strong smell of ammonia from urine filled the air,” said Kaley Pugh, regional manager, animal protection services at the BC SPCA.

The SPCA is now treating the animals for a range of health conditions. All 14 cats and the dog tested positive for ringworm, while the cats also tested positive for roundworm, tapeworm, coccidia, and lungworm.

Ringworm is highly contagious and required the animals to be quarantined, says the SPCA.

“To protect our other animals, this group needed to be isolated, and staff and volunteers need to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) when working with them,” said Leon Davis, regional manager, Islands and Sunshine Coast region.

“In total, this group will need more than a month of dedicated care to recover from their various ailments before we can even start looking for adoptive homes for them.”

While the animals are receiving care, the SPCA says they’re starting to come out of their shells.

Betty, for example, is becoming happier and more affectionate now that she’s undergone extensive grooming to remove the painful mats on her fur.

The cats are also benefiting from socialization and medication, and are “slowly starting to show affection, and interest in their various toys.”

With a long road ahead before the 15 animals are recovered and ready for adoption, the SPCA is looking for donations to help fund their care.

Two SPCA supporters, Sharmini and Anil Wirasekara, have offered to match donations up to $20,000 for the animals’ care. Donations can be made on the BC SPCA website.
